newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ITC suspends panel of directors.
newsitem.headline: India's ITC suspends panel of directors.

text.p: Indian tobacco and hotel conglomerate Indian Tobacco Company (ITC) has suspended its panel of directors, a company spokeswoman said on Friday.

"The committee of directors has been suspended and an interim management committee headed by the chairman of ITC was constituted to run the day-to-day affairs of the company, pending the finalisation of a new management structure," the spokeswoman, Aditi Syam, said in a statement.

India's Enforcement Directorate has arrested several senior ITC officials, as well as two former chairmen, in investigations into alleged violations of India's Foreign Exchange Regulations Act (FERA).
The Finance Ministry said in a recent statement that evidence indicated "violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million."

Friday's announcement followed a meeting of ITC's board of directors in Calcutta, after a decision by two large groups of shareholders in Bombay early this month to review the "corporate culture" of ITC.

These groups include Indian financial institutions, which together hold about 38 percent of ITC's equity, and B.A.T. Industries plc of the U.K., the single largest shareholder, with 31.7 percent of the equity.
Senior B.A.T. officials are also being questioned by the Enforcement Directorate, an arm of India's Finance Ministry.
The ITC statement said the firm's board would be strengthened over the next few weeks by the induction of three independent non-executive directors.
"A board committee was constituted to enquire whether there is prima facie evidence against any of its employees or executive directors of breach of duties to the company," the statement said.
The panel would also recommend changes to the governance, delegated authorities and management structure of the company, it added.
"Executive powers were removed from R K Kutty, F R Vevaina and S Misra, pending the outcome of enquiries by the board committee," the statement said.
Vevaina and Misra are ITC directors who have been arrested by the Enforcement Directorate. Kutty is the director in charge of ITC's international business division.
"Executive powers will immediately be removed from any other executive director/officer of the company arrested or charged by the Enforcement Directorate," the statement said.
The interim management panel would set up a sub-committee to manage all issues related to the firm's current crisis, the statement said.

"The Board has confidence in the intrinsic strength of the company and its people to overcome the crisis," it added. "The Board will extend all support to the authorities for ensuring expeditious resolution of their enquiries."

The ITC committee of directors consists of seven executive directors on the board, which was responsible for the day-to-day affairs of the firm. But the interim management committee will now take over this responsibility.
